kicker: tokin, a gateway for agent RL

scenes.text: The model samples token ids. Its harness keeps only text. So what does the trainer get back?
scenes.say: An agent's model samples token ids. The harness around it keeps only text. So what does the trainer get back?

scenes.headline: How tokin keeps the tokens an agent sampled
scenes.sub: Harnesses speak messages. Reinforcement learning needs token ids.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Rasmus! Coding agents talk in chat messages. Reinforcement learning trains on token ids. Here is how tokin keeps them in step.

scenes.title: Two programs, two languages
scenes.sub: Harnesses speak messages, RL speaks token ids
scenes.say: Chapter one. Two programs, two languages.

steps.term: Harness: the loop around the model
steps.say: A coding agent is two programs. The model samples ids, and the server decodes them to text.
The harness, the loop that runs tools and asks again, keeps only that text.
The next request is text, and the server encodes it again. Nothing promises the same ids come back.
But reinforcement learning needs the exact ids the policy sampled, because that is what the gradient goes through.

scenes.title: Same text, other ids
scenes.sub: Three ways the round trip loses what was sampled
scenes.say: Chapter two. Same text, other ids.

scenes.label: ways the vocabulary can spell the word rollouts
scenes.note: Qwen3.5 tokenizer; the encoder picks one
scenes.say: Qwen three point five can spell the word rollouts a hundred and eighty-nine ways. The model may sample any of them. Re-encoding picks one.

params.top: what the model sampled, with its logprobs
params.bottom: the next request, rendered and encoded again
legend: Sampled: ids and the logprob of each
Canonical text comes back the same
The model drew a split and a blank line: three ids differ
A new user message drops the think block

steps.say: Here is one assistant turn as the model sampled it: a short thought, then a tool call. Each id carries the log probability it was sampled at.
Render the next request and encode it again. When the model sampled the canonical spelling, the same ids come back.
But say the model sampled rollout, then s, and a blank line. Re-encoding gives roll, then outs, and the template trims the blank line. Three ids differ, at the same length, and nothing crashes.
Add a new user message, and the template drops the old thinking. Every later id shifts left, while its recorded log probability stays where it was.

scenes.title: The chat template is a second encoder
scenes.say: The chat template rewrites things too. The article ran Qwen three point five's own template.

items.say: It trims. A blank line the model sampled before the end of its thinking becomes a single line break.
It rebuilds tool calls in its own canonical form.
And when a new user message arrives, it deletes earlier thinking from the prompt. In the article's example, eighteen ids vanish.

scenes.title: What the wrong ids do to the gradient

parts.say: Policy gradients weight each token by a ratio. The bottom was recorded by the sampler, for the id it chose.

parts.note: recomputed on whatever ids it is handed
parts.say: The top is recomputed by the trainer, on whatever ids it is handed.

parts.note: wrong token, wrong context, clipped to a bounded wrong value
parts.say: Hand it re-encoded ids and the ratio compares different tokens. Clipping only bounds the error. And it reinforces a spelling the model never produced.

scenes.title: Token in, token out
scenes.say: Chapter three. Token in, token out.

scenes.text: Sit between harness and engine, keep every sampled id, and encode only the messages that are new.
scenes.mark: encode only the messages that are new
scenes.say: Here's the idea behind tokin. Sit between the harness and the engine. Keep every id the model sampled, and encode only the messages that are new.

scenes.title: Every prefix is token in, token out
scenes.text: next prompt = last prompt + sampled + delta

parts.say: The next prompt starts with the last prompt's stored ids.
Then exactly the ids the model sampled.
Then delta, the new message. That is all tokin ever encodes.

scenes.say: So tokin keeps one rule along every trajectory.

scenes.credit: the launch animation, from a post on X

steps.say: The launch animation shows one request. Attach finds its place in the session. Render locks the sampled ids.
Generate sends ids to the engine and back. Parse returns a message to the harness.
The harness sends its conversation as messages to a session address on tokin.
tokin finds the turn this request continues, and sends the engine its stored ids plus the new messages, encoded.
steps.term: Attach: find the turn a request continues

steps.say: Sampled ids come back with log probabilities. tokin files them in the session's tree and parses a message for the harness.
Each leaf is a rollout: ids, a loss mask and log probabilities, exactly as sampled.
Harnesses retry, edit and compact. Here request D rewrote an observation, so it branches at A and keeps A's sampled ids.
Every root-to-leaf path is one rollout. C and D are this session's two.

scenes.title: Does it help training?
scenes.sub: Real RL gains, not yet credited to fidelity
scenes.say: Chapter four. Does it help training?

scenes.title: Qwen3.8-27B, held-out MiMo pass@1
scenes.note: pi agent trained with slime through tokin
scenes.say: Trained this way, with slime, the dense model went from one half to four fifths on held-out coding tasks.

scenes.title: What the release does not show
scenes.say: The article read the numbers at their sample sizes.

items.say: There is no run of the same recipe through a re-rendering gateway, so nothing measures what token fidelity is worth.
The Terminal-Bench gains sit at the edge of their own noise.
And version zero point one is text only, on SGLang, for four template families.

scenes.text: Never encode what the model sampled: keep the ids, and encode only the new messages.
scenes.say: Never encode what the model sampled. Keep the ids, and encode only what is new.

recap: Each leaf of the tree is a rollout
scenes.say: Re-encoding changes ids. tokin encodes only what is new. Every leaf is a rollout. Thanks for watching!
